thread:
kevin: Quick flag: River13b int4 canary tripped memory fragmentation and a couple of OOMs after a traffic burst; looks tied to KV prefetch + mixed-size batches (many short-turn chats requesting long continuations).
tara: Can you drop a log snippet?
kevin: sure:

```
[2026-04-02T14:08:10Z] alloc_fail: need_contiguous=1.85GB for kv_block
[2026-04-02T14:08:10Z] kv_prefetch: pages=46 page_sz=64KB total_prefetch=2.9MB
[2026-04-02T14:08:10Z] batch: inflight=11 max_new_tokens=768
[2026-04-02T14:08:10Z] allocator: largest_free_segment=740MB free_chunks=30
```

eli: int4 only? fp16 okay?
kevin: fp16 had no failures on same traffic. int4 layout seems to amplify fragmentation.
mina: immediate triage thoughts: 1) lower default max_new_tokens for river13b-int4 to 300, 2) change prefetch to windowed/incremental mode with per-request cap, 3) soft-cap batch size when request asks for >300 tokens.
tara: also consider runtime retry: on failed contiguous alloc, run a short coalesce (<=10ms) and retry once. Might convert OOMs to retries. Ops will want CPU impact estimate.
kevin: quick config I pushed to canary patch: 

```
models:
  river13b-int4:
    defaults:
      max_new_tokens: "300"
      kv_prefetch_mode: "windowed"
      kv_prefetch_window_bytes: "65536"
      kv_prefetch_max_pages: "20"
    batch:
      long_gen_max_batch: "6"
    runtime:
      compaction_on_alloc_ms: "8"
```

alloc-bot: deploy started for river13b-int4 canary (uid: e7c9f)

kevin: 20m in: p95 down ~30%, two alloc failures turned into successful retries after compaction-on-alloc, no hard OOMs. largest_free_segment median rose to ~1.8GB.
eli: nice. Mina, can you add allocator exporters: allocator.largest_free_segment_bytes, allocator.fragmentation_ratio, allocator.coalesce_attempts and hook to dashboard?
mina: on it. also adding an alert if largest_free_segment < 800MB for >45s.
tara: quality check: reducing max_new_tokens may affect rare long-gen calls. How many callers actually request >300?
kevin: traffic analysis: ~0.9% of requests ask for >300 originally. We have a routing rule to send explicit >512 requests to dedicated-large pool; that'll catch heavy users.
eli: follow-ups: - open infra ticket to improve slab merging and avoid large contiguous allocs for KV blocks - investigate quant layout/page alignment tweaks to reduce fragmentation in int4 builds - add nightly stress test that simulates many short turns requesting long continues.
mina: canary run plan: keep overrides for 24h, if stable roll to default and publish short note to users about slightly lower default max_new_tokens for this model and recommended path for very long outputs.
kevin: thanks team. saving artifacts to /incidents/river13b-prefetch-2026-04-02 and updating the onboarding playbook.
